subject: Career
title: Async-First Communication
description: A quick win: understand Async-First Communication.

hook.text: Your teammate is in Tokyo. You're in London. Synchronous communication means someone works at 3 AM.

buildup.text: Async-first means defaulting to messages, docs, and recordings instead of live meetings.

discovery.text: GitLab, a fully remote company of 2,000+, operates almost entirely async with a public handbook.

twist.text: Async isn't slower — it's more thoughtful. People can compose better responses without real-time pressure.

climax.text: Reserve sync (meetings) for brainstorming, sensitive topics, and relationship building. Everything else: async.

punchline.text: Default to async. Escalate to sync when it matters.

quiz.question: What does async-first communication mean?
options: Defaulting to messages and docs instead of live meetings

details.summary: Async-first communication treats written, non-real-time messages as the default channel and reserves synchronous meetings for situations that truly require them. This approach respects time zones, protects deep work, and creates searchable documentation.
details.whyItMatters: Real-time communication fragments attention and excludes distributed team members. Async-first culture enables global collaboration while preserving the focus time that produces high-quality work.
takeaways: Default to written messages and documents over meetings
Reserve synchronous time for relationship building and complex discussion
Create clear norms for expected response times on async channels

faq.question: How do you implement async-first communication without losing team cohesion?
faq.answer: Schedule regular synchronous touchpoints for relationship building, such as weekly team calls and occasional social sessions. Use async for information sharing, decisions with clear criteria, and status updates. The combination preserves connection without the meeting overload.

faq.question: What tools support async-first communication most effectively?
faq.answer: Notion or Confluence for documentation, Loom for video updates, Slack with clear channel conventions for messaging, and Linear or Asana for project tracking. The tools matter less than the cultural norm that writing is the primary communication method.
